Introduction:

The ventura superior court is a city courthouse in the Ventura County. It was established in 1872 and then demolished in 1920; it was again built with a city hall in 1974. The court’s mission is to serve the people with dignity, respect and justice regardless of religion, color, race, etc. It has jurisdiction over criminal, small claims and probation matters and juvenile, civil, family, traffic, and vehicle matters. They provide online services like e-delivery, online payment, forms, online case search inquiry, traffic school, an extension of tickets and many more, so it is optional to go to court for these services. public must follow local rules in this county superior court. The Hall of Justice stands as a symbol of justice and equity, where the rule of law is upheld and experienced where impartiality and fairness prevail in the courtrooms within its walls.

They also provide live audio broadcast streaming experience for certain court proceedings. Proper dressing is required during the case hearing. Three ventura superior courts located in Ventura County are:

  • VENTURA COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – EAST COUNTY COURTHOUSE
  • VENTURA COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – JUVENILE COURTHOUSE
  • VENTURA COUNTY SUPERIOR COURT – VENTURA HALL OF JUSTICE

History of the Superior Court of Ventura

The Superior Court of Ventura has a long and interesting history. The court was first established in 1873, just a few years after Ventura County was formed. The ventura superior court was initially held in a small room in the courthouse, and it was presided over by a single judge. As the county grew, so did the court. Today, the Superior Court of Ventura County has multiple judges, commissioners, and staff, and it operates out of several locations throughout the county superior court. The Hall of Justice serves as the central hub for legal proceedings, where judges, lawyers, and juries convene to uphold justice and administer the law.

Jurisdiction and Authority

The Superior Court of Ventura County has jurisdiction over all civil, criminal, and family law cases within the county. It also has the authority to preside over probate cases, juvenile cases, and small claims cases. The court is responsible for interpreting and enforcing the laws of the state of California within Ventura County. The Hall of Justice stands as a symbol of justice and integrity.

Types of Cases Handled by the Superior Court of Ventura County

The Superior Court of Ventura County handles a wide variety of cases. Here are some of the types of cases that the court handles:

  • Civil cases, such as public injury cases, contract disputes, and property disputes.
  • Criminal cases, such as misdemeanors and felonies.
  • Family law cases, such as divorce, child custody, public health and child support.
  • Juvenile cases, such as delinquency and dependency cases.
  • Probate cases, such as estate administration and will disputes.
  • Small claims cases, such as disputes involving less than $10,000.
  • Traffic school

How can I make a payment?

Superior Court of Ventura County traffic tickets and fines payments can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

public can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court of Ventura County during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the payment center. Take your ticket when you are coming for payment. 2.5% surcharges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card. 

Online

Online traffic tickets or other fines payments can be made using the Superior Court Online Portal of Ventura County superior. Enter the Ticket/Citation, case, and driving license number. Your case information with the amount of the fine will be displayed. Select the payment option and pay the amount online. 

Mail

public can send a certified check or money order to the court’s mailing address; 800 S Victoria Ave, Ventura, CA 93009, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number and account number when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

Drop Box

The payment can also be made by putting the sealed envelope with the case or citation number in the drop box available at the court’s front door or hall of Ventura County superior.

How can I take remote hearing?

Ventura County Superior Court remote hearing request can be done through the zoom application. Some civil, family, traffic and probate-type case hearings findings can be done online. You had to submit a form by filling in all the required information. After receiving the form, the court will email you a schedule and a zoom link. You can join the session with your attorney or lawyer on your Schedule with a link. It is recommended to join the session ten minutes before the actual time. Make sure your internet is working, and test your audio and video before the meeting. On your hearing date, mute your mic until the judge calls your name. Recording and screenshots of the hearing are strictly prohibited due to security. Read all the local rules and meeting information for the zoom session provided by this court of Ventura County or California law.

What will the East County Courthouse do?

Ventura County Superior Court – East County Courthouse collects all the payments of criminal and traffic cases and traffic school. This ventura county superior collects all the traffic, vehicle and speeding ticket payments. Contact county superior court if you have any issues related to the payments and expected website.

How can small claims cases be filled?

Ventura County Superior Court – Ventura Hall of Justice hears all the matters related to small claims cases. The case can be filled by filling out the form received from the clerk’s office and then entering your and the defendant’s personal information like name, phone number and traffic school etc. You had to write the amount you are suing to the defendant and the reason. The defendant must be from this county; only other county public cases cannot be filed there. Contact the court if you need further guidance or help related to these cases. Ventura County Superior Court – Ventura Hall of Justice handles all cases related to family division. The cases include:

  • Divorce, legal separation
  • Child custody and visitation
  • Domestic partnership dissolution and business cases
  • Adoption matters
  • Domestic violence
  • Child support actions

Forms for these cases and matters can be obtained from Ventura County court and the local court form of California website. Contact the court if you need any help. Serving on jury duty is a vital civic responsibility on hall of justice that ensures fair and impartial trials in our court system by law firms.

The Juvenile courthouse handles which types of cases?

Ventura County Superior Court – Juvenile Courthouse handles all the matters of juvenile and probate cases. The juvenile matters include:

  • All offenses that, if committed by an adult, will consider a crime
  • All traffic tickets or violation matters like accidents, speeding and traffic school etc.
  • Protection of children who are mistreated or neglected by the family

All juvenile matters are kept confidential by hall of justice, and case hearings are not done online. The juvenile had to appear with their parents or legal guardian in the case hearing in court of Ventura County superior.

The Traffic Division handles which types of cases?

Ventura County Superior Court- hall of justice handles all the cases related to traffic and vehicle offenses. The cases and violations include:

  •  Accident
  •  Hit and run case
  •  Violation of traffic rules and signals  
  •  Using a Mobile phone during driving
  • Drive without or with an expired license
  •  Speeding
  • Traffic school

Some traffic violation cases are heard remotely in Ventura County, while some can be solved by writing a plea or paying fines only. The fines of the cases depend upon the type of violation a prison committed under Ventura county superior.

How can an adoption petition be filed?

Superior Court of Ventura County family law also handles all matters related to adoption. The petition can be filled by appearing in the court on the Schedule. The adoption is private, so all hearings related to this matter are closed to the public by hall of justice. While you come for the petition, bring the child with you to the court and then the court will decide which is best for the kid. If you want to appear, then an appointment is necessary. If someone wants to apply for a child adoption, they must first file for a step-parent adoption in Ventura County Court.

FAQ:

How can I make an appointment with the clerk?

You can make an appointment with the clerk online by visiting the website and clicking the Schedule an appointment button. 

What happens if I fail to pay my fine on time?

If you fail to pay your fine on time, additional fines will be added to the previous one, your license or insurance will be canceled, and sometimes warrants will be issued against you.
